findings.reason: a worker dispatched an hour after §2 lands will observe almost no after-window traffic and report zero, so the node must be told a volume floor (or a before/after ratio) that can fail.
findings.text: the after-window measure is "held-on-claim verdicts on shared-root file paths at zero", an assertion that is satisfied by an empty or near-empty window, and the section declares no minimum volume of concurrent file claims and no negative control, so a glance at a quiet fleet reads as a pass

findings.reason: §2 as written fixes four of the five instances it argues from and leaves the fifth in place, so either the declaration must cover per-fragment sharing with directory claims, or the plan must say bullet five is out of scope.
findings.text: §1 cites a run claiming a plan's whole docs/evidence/fragments/<plan> directory as one of five blockers, but §2 makes docs/evidence/fragments/ neither a shared root nor an exclusive pattern and keeps every directory claim exclusive, so that cited blocker survives the plan's own remedy

findings.reason: the worker must extend an existing refusal branch rather than add a detection path, and recovery_repair_dispatch.dispatch_repair_for_run composes only from a finding-bearing review record, so §3 needs to name the new non-review source it is adding.
findings.text: §3 states that crew merge refuses a conflicting head "and nothing follows, so the run sits delivered and unlanded", but reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1554 already detects the conflict through _merge_conflicts, records an admission_landing refusal naming the paths on the run and appends an obligation row; what is actually missing is the repair round and a merge-conflict outcome

findings.reason: §1 already enumerates the four modules by name and a grep settles it, so the count costs a turn rather than sending the node to the wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §2's write paths say "the five calling modules where the call site must change", but only four modules call runs._shared_write_paths (dispatch_claims.py x2, promotion_scope.py x2, queue_admission.py x2, queue_edit.py x1); dispatch.py:180 and promotion.py:136 only re-export the symbol

findings.reason: the fragment itself sits on a durable docs/evidence path and the run directory is durable too, so this is a precision gap in the brief rather than a lost record.
findings.text: the commands that produced §4's counts are described as "logged under the run directory", which names no run and therefore no path a later reader can open

response_events.note: §4's done-when now requires the after window to hold at least five pairs of runs with concurrent claims on one shared-root file, and a negative control: the before window must show held-on-claim verdicts on shared-root paths above zero; a quiet window is reported as unmeasured, not as a pass

a new §5 covers the fifth cited blocker: a claim on a plan's evidence-fragments directory is narrowed to the fragment files a node writes, so it never blocks a sibling node of that plan; §2's done-when is unchanged

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §2 names "the five calling modules" where only four call runs._shared_write_paths; every file, symbol and commit the plan cites otherwise resolves, including commit 5cf29445c8, merge.refusing_conflicts and the held-on-claim verdict.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's done-when can pass on an empty measurement, because its measure is a zero with no volume floor. §2 and §3 each name a base-revision negative control and are measurable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §4 writes its counts to a durable docs/evidence/fragments path but places the producing commands "under the run directory" without naming a run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and the merge-conflict outcome name describe the mechanism, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's directory-claim pain is left unfixed by §2's own rules, and §3's premise that "nothing follows" a refused merge is contradicted by the admit lander's existing refusal record.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2, §3 and §4 states one deliverable (one shared-by-default rule, one repair round on a conflicting landing, one measurement).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-section-depends-on resolves s4 to s2 and s3, both of which exist; s2 and s3 declare no dependency and their fixtures can be built by direct calls in a temporary repository, so neither needs the other.
